messages:
molly: Quick note — noticed a bunch of quota / billing surprises this week when teams use delegated service accounts across projects. Idea: add a small 'token lineage' heatmap in Console that shows where a key originated, which proxies/impersonations touched it, and the final project routing so we can debug quota attribution faster.

devon: love the heatmap idea. debugging these by hand is a pain. would be great if it linked to the routing policy that made the decision. :pray:

anya: two quick concerns: 1) provenance info can contain org/project ids — we need redaction options, 2) how do we populate lineage when the proxy strips claims (legacy proxies)?

matt: implementation thought — proxy/edge should emit a signed header we can trust, e.g. `x-rw-provenance: sig=v1;entries=proxy1|impersonate:sa@p:team-b|route:project:billing`. Console and telemetry can verify signature with the proxy public key. that handles untrusted intermediaries.

kevin: signing seems reasonable. for telemetry we'd parse the header and store a compact route fingerprint (sha256) + stable labels (origin, last_impersonator, final_project) so dashboards can aggregate without storing raw ids unless allowed.

molly: yes — store fingerprint + optional human labels controlled by admin setting. UI can show labels only to org admins or when retention policy permits.

anya: what about quota routing fallback when project claim missing? current behavior routes to org default project which caused the surprise. if lineage shows 'no claim' then Console should offer a quick rollback to previous routing policy.

devon: +1. UX needs a one-click drilldown: heatmap -> timeline -> route rule -> rollback/canary link. Keep it tiny in the Console so it doesn't overwhelm.

matt: curious edge: offline/airgapped private deployments can't call our key-signing service. we should allow customers to upload a public key to their control plane or support HSM signing.

kevin: agree. add a config flag `provenance_mode: signed|unsigned|disabled`. signed is default for hosted, but private can choose. telemetry pipeline should reject unsigned if org policy requires signatures.

sre-bot: incident #2412 created: "unexpected org-default quota billing" — linking to this thread.

molly: thanks bot. @kevin @matt can you sketch the telemetry schema? I want the Console heatmap to be live (low-latency) and also have a rollup for weekly billing scans.

kevin: will post a short schema later today. plan: event fields = [fingerprint, origin_type, origin_id_hash, final_project_hash, last_impersonator_hash, signature_verification, route_rule_id, timestamp]. hashes unless admin allows plaintext labels.

matt: quick sample header we experimented with: ```
x-rw-provenance: sig=v1;k=proxy1;s=MEU...;p=origin:api-key|imp:sa:ingest@proj-a|route:proj-b
``` works with our existing signature verification lib.

anya: one more UX ask: Console should surface when a routing policy changed in the last 24h that could explain the spike (can link to rollout history). saves paging eng.

molly: agreed. next steps: kevin/matt take telemetry + header sketch -> eng-platform spike. anya/devon will draft Console mock with minimal controls and admin gating. Ops will test on canary.

devon: tagged for spike: #eng-platform, will add RFC to the repo.

ops-bot: canary cluster scheduled for test on 2024-10-03 22:00 UTC (auto-created by ops-bot).

molly: perfect, thanks everyone. :rocket:
